ownership.note: Reusable platform packages. The Template source owns updates here.
Auth is sensitive in our Derived project. Overlaps with packages/** — engine MUST warn and treat this rule as more specific.
Environment contract is platform-owned and synced as Template source content.
Product-specific environment example. Distinct from the Environment contract and must not be overwritten.
Product domain: checkout flow. The Template source never edits these files; conflicts must be reported.
Mixed ownership via two Sync seams: api-route-registration (issue #31) and product-route-registration (issue #35). Engine preserves registerRoute(...) and registerProductRoute(...) calls.
Mixed ownership via the product-module-registration Sync seam (issue #35). Engine preserves registerProductModule(...) calls.

Mixed ownership but no Sync seam is registered for this file in v1.1.0. The Derived project already has its own version; the Template source v1.2.0 also adds one. Engine MUST report this as a conflict and not silently merge. Issue #35 documents this as the negative case that justifies the new product-module-registration seam on apps/api/products.ts.
Catch-all for app scaffolding owned by the Template source. The more specific apps/checkout/**, apps/api/routes.ts, apps/api/products.ts, and apps/api/middleware.ts rules win precedence.

Derived-project lockfile. Engines MUST regenerate this locally after a Template update; the Template source does NOT ship a lockfile. Engines must never copy the Template source's lockfile into the Derived project.

seams.note: Derived projects register generic routes inside this seam without editing the surrounding harness. Issue #31.

Derived projects register Product domain routes (checkout, catalogue, etc.) inside this seam. Issue #35 separates Product domain routes from generic platform routes so the seam responsibility is clear and zone markers are not required.

Derived projects register Product domain modules (request-time logic, feature flags, audits) inside this seam. Issue #35 turns the existing lncd module-wiring drift into an explicit extension point so middleware-style concerns route through the seam instead of editing apps/api/middleware.ts directly.

environmentContract.note: Template-owned platform environment requirements. Synced as Template source content and regenerated on update.
